title: Unary comparison language
statement: Let $	ext{pairEncode}$ denote the pairing of two Boolean words into one Boolean word. Define a language over the Boolean alphabet by including exactly those words that can be written as $	ext{pairEncode}(1^n,	ext{bits}(i))$ for natural numbers $n$ and $i$ with $i<n$, where $1^n$ is the length-$n$ word consisting entirely of true symbols and $	ext{bits}(i)$ is the binary representation of $i$.
caveat: The snippet uses pairEncode without defining it, so its encoding convention cannot be specified more precisely here.
